content.title: Web: add a configured product with quantity {{valid_quantity_n}} and confirm cart count, subtotal, and quantity carry over

check.operand: header cart item count equals the previous cart item count plus the entered quantity

content.test_md_blob:
# Web: add a configured product with quantity {{valid_quantity_n}} and confirm cart count, subtotal, and quantity carry over

> Prove that a shopper can add a valid product after selecting required options, receive a success confirmation, see the header cart signals update, and have the entered non-1 quantity carry into the cart exactly.

## Step 1

At {{start_url}}, open a product listing that contains {{product_with_required_options}}; store the current header cart item count as baseline_header_count and the current header cart subtotal as baseline_header_subtotal, then open {{product_with_required_options}} from that listing.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-16

On the product detail page for {{product_with_required_options}}, in the purchase section, select every required option and enter {{valid_quantity_n}} in the quantity field, then assert the quantity field is present and shows {{valid_quantity_n}}.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-17, ac-12

From the same purchase section, add the configured product to the cart, then assert the add completes successfully and a success confirmation is shown.

## Step 4 @verifies ac-7, ac-8, ac-9

Open the cart and inspect the line for {{product_with_required_options}}, then assert the cart quantity equals {{valid_quantity_n}}, the header cart item count equals baseline_header_count plus {{valid_quantity_n}}, and the header cart subtotal equals the cart subtotal shown on the cart page.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: At {{start_url}}, open a product listing that contains {{product_with_required_options}}; store the current header cart item count as baseline_header_count and the current header cart subtotal as baseline_header_subtotal, then open {{product_with_required_options}} from that listing.
    step: 1
  - objective: On the product detail page for {{product_with_required_options}}, in the purchase section, select every required option and enter {{valid_quantity_n}} in the quantity field, then assert the quantity field is present and shows {{valid_quantity_n}}.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-16
  - objective: From the same purchase section, add the configured product to the cart, then assert the add completes successfully and a success confirmation is shown.
    step: 3
    verifies:
      - ac-17
      - ac-12
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: propagation
      operand: header cart item count equals the previous cart item count plus the entered quantity
      operator: equals
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-8
    objective: Open the cart and inspect the line for {{product_with_required_options}}, then assert the cart quantity equals {{valid_quantity_n}}, the header cart item count equals baseline_header_count plus {{valid_quantity_n}}, and the header cart subtotal equals the cart subtotal shown on the cart page.
    step: 4
    verifies:
      - ac-7
      - ac-8
      - ac-9
scenario: Add a configured product with a valid non-1 quantity and see the cart update correctly
title: 'Web: add a configured product with quantity {{valid_quantity_n}} and confirm cart count, subtotal, and quantity carry over'

content.title: Web: block add to cart when a required product option is missing

check.operand: successful add-to-cart completion before all required options are selected

content.test_md_blob:
# Web: block add to cart when a required product option is missing

> Prove that add to cart is blocked until required options are selected and that the shopper is told which required option is missing.

## Step 1

At {{start_url}}, open a product listing that contains {{product_with_required_options}} and open {{product_with_required_options}} from that listing.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-10, ac-11

On the product detail page for {{product_with_required_options}}, leave one required option unselected and attempt to add the product to the cart, then assert the page identifies the specific missing required option and no successful add-to-cart completion is shown.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: At {{start_url}}, open a product listing that contains {{product_with_required_options}} and open {{product_with_required_options}} from that listing.
    step: 1
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: forbidden-presence
      operand: successful add-to-cart completion before all required options are selected
      operator: exists
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-10
    objective: On the product detail page for {{product_with_required_options}}, leave one required option unselected and attempt to add the product to the cart, then assert the page identifies the specific missing required option and no successful add-to-cart completion is shown.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-10
      - ac-11
scenario: Attempt to add a product while a required option is still missing
title: 'Web: block add to cart when a required product option is missing'

content.title: Web: open a product from a listing and verify its buying information is shown

check.operand: product price on the product detail page

content.test_md_blob:
# Web: open a product from a listing and verify its buying information is shown

> Prove that opening a product from a listing reveals the product information a shopper needs to decide whether to buy.

## Step 1

At {{start_url}}, open a product listing and open any listed product from that page.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-13, ac-14, ac-15, ac-16

On the product detail page for the opened product, inspect the product summary and purchase section, then assert the product name, product price, availability, and a quantity field are shown.
content.objectives_blob:
objectives:
  - objective: At {{start_url}}, open a product listing and open any listed product from that page.
    step: 1
  - check:
      expected_mode: authored
      kind: presence
      operand: product price on the product detail page
      operator: exists
      review_required: false
      verified_against: ac-13
    objective: On the product detail page for the opened product, inspect the product summary and purchase section, then assert the product name, product price, availability, and a quantity field are shown.
    step: 2
    verifies:
      - ac-13
      - ac-14
      - ac-15
      - ac-16
scenario: Open a product from a listing and inspect its buying information
title: 'Web: open a product from a listing and verify its buying information is shown'

judgements.rationale: [self_critique] Oracle fit: the test proved quantity carryover by reading the cart line and proved header count/subtotal with explicit baseline capture and comparison, so the checks observed the promised outcomes rather than the click itself. Technique fit: representative valid configured-product coverage matched the happy-path promise and did not invent quantity bounds. Negative coverage existed separately in sc-2. Assert breadth was limited to the specific success confirmation, carried quantity, header count change, and header/cart subtotal equality.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the test proved the blocked-add promise by asserting the missing required option was identified and that successful add completion was absent after the attempt. Technique fit: negative/error coverage matched the required-option gate promise. The complementary happy path existed separately in sc-1, so the family had both positive and negative coverage. Assert breadth stayed narrow to the missing-option identification and absence of successful add completion.

[self_critique] Oracle fit: the test observed only the four display promises named in the source on the product detail page. Technique fit: a simple representative rendering path was sufficient because the scenario had no independent outcome-changing inputs. Negative coverage was intentionally not attached here because the source did not promise invalid product-opening behavior in this use case. Assert breadth stayed limited to presence of name, price, availability, and quantity field without inferring any cart behavior.
